scenes.title: Facebook leads already in GoHighLevel
scenes.page: Lesson 2 • Keep your existing Facebook connection
scenes.narration: This lesson is for Facebook or Instagram Instant Forms whose leads already arrive in Go High Level. We won't reconnect an integration that's working. Instead, we'll send the right form's new leads from Go High Level into Patient Pipeline. We'll create the campaign, add one sending workflow, and walk through the checks. The outside-service screens are labeled recreations, not recordings of your accounts. Pause after each step as needed.

fields.label: Before starting
fields.value: New Instant Form leads already arrive in the correct practice

scenes.checkpoint: If leads do not reach GoHighLevel, this is not your route.

scenes.title: Before we begin
scenes.narration: Before we start, have your actual offer beside you, and make sure you can sign in to the accounts this lesson uses. You'll need permission to edit the connection. Keep Patient Pipeline open in one browser tab and the other service in another. The little plus sign opens a new tab without closing your work. For testing, use your own name and a phone number you control. Existing emails or texts may run, so let your office know you're doing a setup check. Pause here until you're ready.

fields.label: Account access
fields.value: Patient Pipeline Lead Follow-Up and the source service

fields.label: Test information
fields.value: Your own name and phone; no patient information

scenes.checkpoint: Sign in before continuing. Never show passwords or private links.

scenes.title: Confirm the page and Instant Form
scenes.narration: Before adding the new connection, find a recent lead from this exact Facebook or Instagram form in Go High Level. Check the name and phone. Write down the Facebook Page name and the Instant Form name used by this offer. An Instagram business account uses its linked Facebook Page for this connection. If the lead never reached Go High Level, pause here and fix that first connection. We shouldn't build the next step on top of a missing first step.

fields.label: Contacts
fields.value: Confirm an actual recent lead and phone

scenes.checkpoint: No sample contact shown here is proof that your existing integration works.

scenes.title: Open a new campaign
scenes.narration: Let's start in Patient Pipeline. Choose Lead Follow-Up, rather than Reactivation. Then open Campaigns. On the Campaigns page, click New Campaign. A campaign is the offer that brought someone to your practice. We're going to use the same campaign all the way through this lesson, so the connection and the test stay together. Pause here when the new campaign form is open.
scenes.checkpoint: You should be in Lead Follow-Up, with New Campaign open.

scenes.title: Choose the service
scenes.narration: Click Service type to open the list. Choose the service your ad actually promotes. We're choosing Chiropractic for our back pain example. If your offer is for another service, choose that instead. This choice determines which call script your team will use. Check the selected service before moving on. You don't have to copy our example if it doesn't match your practice.
scenes.checkpoint: The selected service must match your ad.

scenes.title: Type a recognizable name
scenes.narration: Now click Campaign name. Give this offer a name your team will recognize. We're typing Back Pain Relief, forty-nine-dollar New Patient Special. You can see the words appearing in the field as we type them. For your campaign, use your own offer name. Keep it specific enough that you can recognize it when we return to check the test.

fields.label: Campaign name
fields.value: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

actions.result: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special

scenes.checkpoint: Use the same campaign for setup, connection, and testing.

scenes.title: Enter what the offer includes
scenes.narration: Under What's included in the offer, enter one item on each line. Our example has a consultation, an examination, and a review of findings. Click the first row and type the first item. Use Add a line for another row, then enter the next item. These details become part of what the caller says, so only include what your ad really promises. Pause and compare your entries with the offer.
scenes.checkpoint: One real included item per row.

scenes.title: Choose Just Y, then type 49
scenes.narration: For our example, we only want to say the offer price. Click the middle choice, Just Y. Then click Offer price and type 49. Look at the On the call preview: it now says Just forty-nine dollars. That's the wording your caller will use. This does not change your software bill. If your ad compares a regular price with the offer, use Normally X, now Y and enter both real prices instead. For this example, we'll keep Just Y.
scenes.checkpoint: Just Y selected • Offer price 49 • Preview Just $49

scenes.title: Save and connect leads
scenes.page: Back Pain Relief — $49 New Patient Special
scenes.narration: Leave the expiration or limited-spots box blank unless your offer really has that restriction. Check your service, campaign name, included items, and price once more. Now click Save and Connect Leads. Wait for the campaign's setup page to open. Saving stores your offer, but it doesn't connect the form by itself. We'll make that connection next. Keep this campaign open in its browser tab.
scenes.checkpoint: Wait until the saved campaign's connection setup opens.

scenes.title: Copy this campaign's address
scenes.narration: In the campaign setup, choose Go High Level. Find this campaign's private connection address and click its Copy button. Don't copy the ordinary page address from the top of your browser. This special address tells the other service where to send the lead. Keep it private, and don't put it in your ad. We're hiding it in this lesson. You'll paste your own full address into the connection shortly.
scenes.checkpoint: Copy the special campaign address—not the browser's page URL.

scenes.title: Create a separate workflow
scenes.narration: Click your Go High Level browser tab. Check that you're in the right practice. Open Automation, then Workflows. Click Create Workflow and choose Start from scratch. We're making a separate connection workflow so we don't change your existing follow-up messages. Click the workflow name and type Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline. Use a name that identifies your own form. Pause here when the new workflow is open.

fields.label: Workflow name
fields.value: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

actions.result: Send Back Pain Form to Patient Pipeline

scenes.checkpoint: Use a new workflow, not an existing messaging sequence.

scenes.title: Use Facebook Lead Form Submitted
scenes.narration: Click Add New Trigger and search for Facebook Lead Form Submitted. Choose that exact trigger. This is different from Form Submitted, which is for forms built inside Go High Level. Add the Page Is filter and select your connected Facebook Page. Then add Form Is and choose this offer's exact Instant Form. Check both names before you click Save Trigger. Without those filters, unrelated forms can enter the wrong campaign.
scenes.checkpoint: Facebook Lead Form Submitted • Page Is • Form Is

scenes.title: Choose Webhook—not Custom Webhook
scenes.narration: Click the plus sign below your saved trigger. In the action search, type webhook. Choose the ordinary action called Webhook, not Custom Webhook and not an inbound webhook. This is the step that sends contact information out to Patient Pipeline. If the screen asks you to buy something or doesn't show this action, stop and check your account's access. Don't choose a different action just because its name is similar.
scenes.checkpoint: Select the standard outbound Webhook action.

scenes.title: Set POST and paste the address
scenes.narration: Name the action Send lead to Patient Pipeline. Open Method and choose POST. Then click inside URL and paste the campaign address you copied. On Windows, hold Control and press V. On a Mac, hold Command and press V. If you copied something else in between, switch back to Patient Pipeline, click Copy again, then return here. The whole private address goes in this URL box. Don't type the example text shown in this lesson.
scenes.checkpoint: Method POST • URL is your campaign's full private address.

scenes.title: Save the sending step
scenes.narration: For this basic connection, leave Headers and Custom Data empty. The standard Webhook action already sends the contact's name and phone, so you don't need to type code or map those ordinary contact fields here. Click Save Action. You should now see your form trigger followed by one Webhook step. We are not adding an email, text message, or phone call to this workflow.
scenes.checkpoint: One form trigger → one Webhook action. No handwritten JSON.

scenes.title: Allow re-entry, save, and publish
scenes.narration: Open the workflow's Settings tab. Turn on Allow Re-entry for this new connection workflow. That lets someone submit again after their previous run has finished. Return to the Builder and click Save. Now change Draft to Publish. If another save indicator appears, click Save again. Saved and published are different: one stores the instructions, and the other allows them to run. Check both before testing.
scenes.checkpoint: Saved AND Published. This demonstration has not activated your account.

scenes.title: Send a new form submission
scenes.narration: Now open the actual ad or its form preview and complete the same Instant Form a new lead would use. Use your own contact details and read the required consent information. Submit once after the workflow is published. For an end-to-end live-ad check, use the form through the actual ad. Meta's Lead Ads Testing Tool can help with a setup test, but its test leads are not proof that a particular live ad works.
scenes.checkpoint: Use the exact form after publishing. Test-tool data is a separate setup check.

scenes.title: Follow the lead through GoHighLevel
scenes.narration: Return to Go High Level and open Contacts. Find the new test person and match the phone number. Then open the connection workflow and its Execution Logs. Look for the same contact and a recent run of the Webhook step. Running Test Workflow with an old contact is not the same test: it bypasses the new Facebook form submission we're checking. Once this new lead has reached Go High Level, continue to Patient Pipeline.

fields.label: Find your test
fields.value: Match the actual name and phone

scenes.checkpoint: Trace the same new submission, not an unrelated old contact.

scenes.title: Check the receipt, then the lead
scenes.narration: After your real form submission, return to the same campaign in Patient Pipeline. Look for a recent Form submission received message. If it still says it's waiting, give it a moment and refresh the page with your browser's circular-arrow button. Then open this campaign's Leads tab. Match the name and phone you entered. The illustration here is showing where to check, not claiming that a live connection has passed.

fields.label: Latest receipt
fields.value: Waiting for a submission from your form

scenes.checkpoint: No success is assumed. Find your own submission in this campaign.

scenes.title: Recognize a successful repeat test
scenes.narration: For a closer check, open Lead sources and look under Last twenty received. Match the delivery time to your test. New lead means a new entry was created. Updated lead can also be successful: that phone number was already in this campaign. A repeat test may not add another row or move the old one to the top. Rejected means something needs fixing. Open that receipt and read the reason before changing settings.

scenes.checkpoint: Status explanations—not a fabricated delivery log.

scenes.title: Don't mistake an internal test for proof
scenes.page: Only want to check our side?
scenes.narration: There are shortcuts that check only part of the connection. Patient Pipeline's internal test checks its own intake. A connector's test action checks a sending step. Neither proves that a new submission to your actual form will arrive automatically. That's why our final check starts with the form itself and ends with the matching campaign lead. Your test entry is a real lead, so let your caller know which entry was the setup check.

fields.label: Connector action test
fields.value: Can send real data; does not prove the trigger

scenes.checkpoint: Keep private details out of screenshots and shared troubleshooting messages.

scenes.title: Find which connection needs attention
scenes.narration: If your test is absent from Go High Level, check the existing Facebook integration, the Page and form selection, and the name and phone field mapping. The account owner may need to restore leads access. If the test is in Go High Level but not Patient Pipeline, check the new workflow's Page Is and Form Is filters, its published status, and the Webhook execution. Fix the first missing part. Don't disconnect a working integration just to start over.

fields.value: Check Facebook integration, permissions, and field mapping

fields.label: Present in GoHighLevel
fields.value: Check trigger filters and published workflow

fields.value: Check POST and the campaign destination

scenes.checkpoint: Settings → Integrations → Facebook Form Fields Mapping, when needed.

scenes.title: Before you call it ready
scenes.narration: Before you call this ready, check four things. Your campaign matches the offer. Your connection watches the right form and is turned on. You submitted that actual form after turning it on. And your matching test entry appears in this campaign. Leave the connection active, and make sure your team knows which entry was the test. One successful test confirms that delivery; it isn't a guarantee that every future delivery will work. You now know where to check.
